visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) A woman with short, dark hair and bangs, wearing a light blue vertical-striped button-down shirt, stands in an indoor setting. Behind her is a white shelving unit holding numerous dark and clear perfume bottles. She looks directly at the camera, gesturing with her right hand while speaking. A yellow text overlay appears at the bottom. (2) The scene cuts to a close-up of a brown glass perfume bottle with a white label and black bulbous cap, held by the woman's hands with pale green nail polish. Text overlays the bottle. She then unscrews the cap, holds the bottle, and brings the cap to her nose to smell it, while gesturing with her free hand. (3) A still image of Japanese actress Haruka Ayase appears, showing her from the shoulders up against a neutral background. Her name is displayed in white text. (4) The woman returns, holding a clear glass bottle with a black cap. Text identifies the brand as Pleuvoir. She continues to speak and gesture, pointing to the bottle and smelling the cap to describe its scent profile. (5) A still image of the singer Rosé appears, leaning against a railing at night with city lights in the background, wearing a black cutout dress. (6) The woman is shown again holding a clear circular perfume bottle from the brand Nonfiction. She smells the cap and speaks enthusiastically, using her hands to emphasize her points about the fragrance's notes. (7) A still image of actor Greg Hsu appears, wearing a blue and white varsity jacket and smiling broadly at an outdoor event. (8) The woman holds a distinctive textured glass bottle from Hotel Dawson. She mimics raindrops falling with her fingers and speaks expressively, describing the scent's evocative nature. (9) A still image of a young Takeshi Kaneshiro appears, wearing a white shirt and winking at the camera with text indicating his name.

narrative_and_purpose.mainPurpose: The video serves as a beauty recommendation guide focusing on four specific Korean perfume brands. The creator uses a 'persona mapping' strategy, associating each scent with a well-known celebrity (Haruka Ayase, Rosé, Greg Hsu, Takeshi Kaneshiro) to provide a tangible and relatable reference for the fragrance's character. This helps viewers visualize the scent's appeal beyond just olfactory descriptions.
